profile.a: The author, writing individually for Strategy, assessing another study group's presentation (Strategy-40).
The course assessors, and in effect Meta's strategy team as the owner of the plan being tested.
Whether Strategy-40, Meta's AI plan built on open-weight Llama models, passes as good strategy.
Handed in on 10 March 2025; the plan rests on Meta's $65bn AI infrastructure spend in 2025.
The global generative AI market, against Google and DeepSeek.
In the 'AI wars' Meta bets on giving models away while monetising attention through ads; the question is whether that bet is defensible.
VRIO with the discover-design-pursue imperatives, direct and indirect network effects, and Rumelt's test of good and bad strategy.

charts.title: Strengths and weaknesses the paper finds in each test
charts.takeaway: The strategy is strongest on imitability and direct network effects (data and 3.4bn users) and weakest on rarity and on the indirect ecosystem, where the plan says what it wants but not how.
charts.source: Count of the points listed under each heading, pages 75-81.

charts.title: The money behind the plan ($bn)
charts.takeaway: Funding is to come from cash, debt and asset sales, but the paper finds the plan explains the spend superficially: it does not show how more data centres become more value for users of the three apps.

items.title: Invest $65bn in AI infrastructure
items.text: Use Llama to improve ad personalisation, content delivery and engagement.

items.title: Commoditise general models
items.text: Open weights for generalist AI, specialist tools for ads and content.

items.title: Expand platforms
items.text: AR/VR, shopping, search and assistants; joint ventures or acquisitions.

items.title: Fund it
items.text: Cash reserves, debt financing and asset sales.

charts.title: Rumelt's test applied

items.title: Clear diagnosis
items.text: Meta's advantage lies in data, scale and network effects.

items.title: Guiding policy
items.text: Commoditise generalist models, specialise in ad tech.

items.title: Coherent actions
items.text: Investments are named, but cloud versus own-compute choices look inconsistent.

items.title: Competitive advantage
items.text: Strong network effects; uniqueness challenged by Google and DeepSeek.

items.title: Implementation plan
items.text: Regulation, retention and ecosystem governance are mentioned without an execution plan.

items.title: Adaptability
items.text: Blue-ocean moves into open-source AI and the metaverse.

charts.takeaway: A clear diagnosis with thin execution: the paper's 'medium strength' verdict follows from the missing implementation detail.
